goal: Let a user upload one or more .gpx GPS track files and have each become a normal flight record in this app. The importer parses the track, resamples it to the app's own point cadence, derives the per-point fields GPS does not carry (ground speed, heading, vertical speed), resolves departure/arrival ICAO with the existing findNearestAirport(), and writes the flight through the existing insertFlight/insertPoint/closeFlight path so the result is indistinguishable downstream from a SimConnect-recorded flight: it lists on Home, renders on the existing map and altitude chart, edits, deletes, exports to PDF, attaches to a trip and links to a planned leg with no special-cased UI. A new flights.source column ('simconnect' | 'gpx') records provenance so an imported flight can be labelled and so live-recording assumptions are never silently applied to a track that was never live.
frozen_decisions: Add a column to `flights` (e.g. `source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'simconnect'`, value `'gpx'` for imports) so the UI can label an imported flight and so duration/interruption logic that assumes a live SimConnect recording (pause detection, active-trip auto-linking's "just took off" checks) isn't silently misapplied to a track that was never live. This is a schema change — routes this run through the Design step, not just Plan -> Implement.

Reuse the existing write path. The importer should call the same `insertFlight` / `insertPoint` / `closeFlight` functions `flightManager.ts` uses (`src/db.ts:313,321,371`), not a parallel write path — it synthesizes the same shape of finalized flight from a static point list instead of a live state machine.
Departure/arrival ICAO via the existing `findNearestAirport()` (`src/airports.ts:102`) on the track's first/last points — identical to the live flow.
No aircraft type in GPX. The upload form takes an optional free-text aircraft field (flights already support editing this after the fact, so it is not blocking).

Computed fields with no GPX source data (airspeed, heading, vertical speed, on-ground) are derived from consecutive trackpoints (bearing, distance/time, altitude delta/time) the same way the live recorder would — `on_ground` has no reliable signal from GPS alone and defaults to false for imported points.

Point density. Phone-recorded GPX tracks are commonly 1-second interval; the app's own recording writes one point per `RECORD_INTERVAL_MS` (5s, `flightManager.ts`). Open question for the Planner/Designer: import at native resolution, or resample to ~5s to match existing chart/map assumptions and keep `flight_points` row counts consistent with SimConnect-recorded flights. Recommend resampling for consistency.

Endpoint and upload conventions follow the `.lnmpln` precedent (`src/server.ts:426-546`, `uploadLnmpln` multer instance at `src/server.ts:24-27`): a dedicated small-file-size multer instance, XML content sniff, per-file try/parse/insert, a batch response shape `{imported, results}` with one entry per file (`status`, `flight_id` or `error`). Proposed route: `POST /api/flights/import/gpx`.

Client entry point follows the `TripDetail.tsx` `.lnmpln` import precedent (`TripDetail.tsx:158-202`) but lives on the Home page (a GPX import isn't tied to a trip) — file input (`accept=".gpx"`, multiple), optional aircraft/notes field, `FormData` POST, per-file result list, refresh the flight list afterward.
Parsing library. `fast-xml-parser` is already a dependency (used by `src/lnmpln.ts`) and GPX is XML — reuse it rather than adding a new GPX parsing dependency.

Duplicate import. Out of scope for v1: re-importing the same file twice creates two flights. (`.lnmpln`'s SHA-256 dedupe is for planned legs, a different table with different semantics — not reused here unless the Planner flags it as needed.)
Ship (DevOps) is skipped: this run touches no build, packaging, or deploy config. No new npm dependency is added.
planner_notes_on_frozen_decisions: Decision 6 (point density) is the one decision the intake left genuinely open. This plan closes it: RESAMPLE, and T-001 must write the exact rule into design.md §4. Rationale: `combineFlights` (src/db.ts:604) synthesizes filler points on the assumption of a coarse cadence, the altitude chart and Leaflet polyline are sized for a few hundred points, and a 4-hour 1 Hz phone track is ~14,400 rows against ~2,900 for the same flight recorded live. Decimation (emit the first real fix at or after each 5 s boundary), never interpolation, so every stored point is a real GPS fix.

Decision 7 is followed with ONE sizing exception, flagged not overridden: `MAX_LNMPLN_BYTES` is 512 KB, which is correct for a few-KB flight plan and too small for a GPX track (a 1 Hz 4-hour track is comfortably 2-5 MB of XML). T-001 must set a separate `MAX_GPX_BYTES` and a hard cap on trackpoints per file, and state both numbers. The `.lnmpln` pattern (own multer instance, own limit) is preserved; only the number differs.

No blocker found for decision 9. `fast-xml-parser` is already configured for attribute parsing in src/lnmpln.ts:270-287 (`ignoreAttributes: false`, `attributeNamePrefix: '@_'`), which is exactly what GPX needs since trkpt lat/lon are attributes. GPX gets its OWN XMLParser instance in src/gpx.ts with its own `isArray` jpaths — src/lnmpln.ts is not touched by this run.

src/gpx.ts must import haversineNm/bearingDeg from src/geo.ts and must NOT import ./db or ./airports — src/geo.ts:9-14 states this rule for exactly this situation, and it is what keeps the module pure enough for a CLI inspector.

`MAX_COUNTED_GAP_MS` (60_000) is exported from src/flightManager.ts:15, but importing it would drag ./db into the pure module. Copy the constant into src/gpx.ts with a comment naming flightManager.ts:15 as the source of truth, the same deliberate-copy idiom src/geo.ts uses.
sequencing_rationale: Two phases, because there are exactly two seams. Phase 1 is 'the server can turn a .gpx into a flight' — provable by curl and a CLI inspector, and already user-visible because the imported flight renders on the existing Home list, map and altitude chart. Phase 2 is 'the user can do it from a button' plus the provenance label. Nothing else in this feature has a seam worth a phase.

The risky part is not the upload plumbing — that is a straight copy of the .lnmpln endpoint — it is the pure transform: metres-to-feet, timestamp normalisation, resampling, derived speed/heading/vertical-speed, and the duration rule. That transform is isolated in src/gpx.ts with zero DB or Express imports and its own inspector src/inspect-gpx.ts, so every number it produces is falsifiable from the command line against checked-in fixtures, with no server, no database and no test framework.

T-002 (pure module) precedes T-003 (schema + endpoint) rather than running beside it, so that each task leaves the tree type-checking on its own. Running them in parallel would leave src/server.ts importing a src/gpx.ts that does not exist yet, and neither dispatcher could then verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`. Parallelism here would buy wall-clock and cost the ability to check the work.

The schema migration and the endpoint are ONE task, not two, because splitting them puts two dispatchers on files that must agree about the same contract (whether insertFlight takes a source argument, or the endpoint stamps it after). One owner, one diff, one review.

The phase-1 reviewer is opus: this phase adds a column to the user's live flights table, and a migration that runs on their real logbook the next time they restart. That is the exact case CLAUDE.md reserves opus review for.

The escape-hatch rule is satisfied by construction: an imported flight uses only the existing manual paths (edit aircraft, attach to trip, manually link a planned leg). Nothing in this run acts automatically. design.md §9 must state that a GPX import deliberately does NOT run the active-trip auto-link, so the automation is never reached without a user action.

T-001 exists because this run introduces three contracts at once — a schema column, a new endpoint, and a shared type mirrored into the client. Freezing them in one document is cheaper than discovering the disagreement in review.

phases.name: GPX becomes a flight: pure transform, schema, endpoint
phases.ships: A .gpx file can be turned into a real flight two ways: `npx ts-node src/inspect-gpx.ts track.gpx` prints exactly the flight that would be created (route, duration, distance, max altitude, resampled point count) without touching a database, and `curl -F gpx=@track.gpx localhost:PORT/api/flights/import/gpx` creates it for real, after which it appears in GET /api/flights and renders on the existing flight detail page, map and altitude chart with no client change at all.

phases.name: Upload from the UI, and say where a flight came from
phases.ships: A user on the Home page picks one or more .gpx files, optionally types an aircraft name, uploads, sees a per-file result list, and the flight table refreshes with the new flights in it. Imported flights carry a visible 'GPX' badge on Home and on the flight detail page so a track that was never flown in the sim is never mistaken for one that was. README documents the feature.

tasks.goal: Write .claude/runs/2026-09-07-gpx-import/design.md as a numbered-section document that every downstream task cites by slice. It must close every question a dispatcher would otherwise guess at: the exact DDL and migration idiom for flights.source, the ParsedGpxTrack type and its reject/warning codes, the resampling rule, the per-point derivation formulas, how the flight summary row is computed, the REST surface, the client contract, and how an imported flight interacts with combineFlights, auto-linking, journey and PDF export. Section numbering is load-bearing: T-002 will be handed `ctx.sh design 2026-09-07-gpx-import 3 4 5 6 10` and T-003 `ctx.sh design 2026-09-07-gpx-import 2 6 7 9`, so the numbering below is fixed, not a suggestion.
acceptance_criteria: design.md exists with exactly these top-level numbered sections, in this order: §1 Scope and what an imported flight is; §2 Schema change: flights.source; §3 GPX parse contract; §4 Resampling; §5 Per-point derivation; §6 Flight summary; §7 REST surface; §8 Client contract; §9 Interaction with existing features; §10 Fixtures. `.claude/tools/ctx.sh design 2026-09-07-gpx-import 2` through `... 10` each print exactly one section.

§2 gives the literal ALTER statement and the guard around it, in the PRAGMA table_info(flights) + ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN idiom already used at src/db.ts:237-271, and states where in initDb() it goes. It confirms that `ALTER TABLE flights ADD COLUMN source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'simconnect'` is legal in SQLite (non-null constant default) and therefore backfills every existing row without a data migration. It states whether a CHECK constraint is used and why (an ADD COLUMN cannot carry one — say so rather than leaving it implied).

§2 states whether `source` is written by a new parameter on insertFlight() or by a separate stamping call after insert, and names the resulting signature verbatim. It states that the SimConnect path (src/flightManager.ts:240) is either unchanged or changed in exactly one named way, and that no existing insertFlight call site is left passing a positional argument in a shifted slot.
§2 declares `source: 'simconnect' | 'gpx'` as a field on the Flight interface in BOTH src/types.ts:27-53 and client/src/types.ts:8-35, and states that the two must stay mirrored.

§3 declares the `ParsedGpxTrack` TypeScript interface (parser output: an ordered array of {ts (ISO UTC string), lat, lon, altitudeFt} plus track name, source filename, and warnings[]) and states that it lives in src/gpx.ts, not src/types.ts, so the pure module owns its own output shape.

§3 gives the fast-xml-parser configuration for GPX verbatim, including the `isArray` jpaths needed so that a file with one <trk>, one <trkseg> or one <trkpt> still parses to arrays, and states the decision on namespace-prefixed documents (`<gpx:trk>`) — either `removeNSPrefix: true` or an explicit reject.

§3 resolves each of these format traps with a named rule, and each rule names the reject code or warning code it produces: (a) lat/lon arrive as XML ATTRIBUTES and as strings under `parseAttributeValue: false`; (b) <ele> is METRES per the GPX schema and must be converted to feet (state the factor); (c) <ele> missing on some or all points; (d) <time> missing on some or all points; (e) multiple <trk> elements and multiple <trkseg> elements in one file; (f) <trkpt> vs <wpt> vs <rtept> — which are read and which are ignored; (g) GPX 1.0 <speed>/<course> and GPX 1.1 <extensions> — state that they are ignored and that everything is derived, per frozen decision 5; (h) timestamps with an offset or fractional seconds, normalised to ISO-8601 UTC because everything else in this tree stores `new Date().toISOString()`; (i) out-of-order, duplicate or equal timestamps (dt = 0 would divide by zero in §5); (j) BOM and the leading-'<' content sniff, reusing the looksLikeXml() rule at src/server.ts:35-39; (k) fewer than 2 trackpoints after filtering.

§3 lists every reject code as a stable UPPERCASE identifier with the one-line human message that accompanies it, in the style of LnmplnRejectCode (src/lnmpln.ts:28-37), and states that a reject throws a `GpxParseError` carrying the code — never a bare Error and never a stack trace to the user.

§4 states the resampling decision as FROZEN (resample, do not import at native resolution), gives the target interval in ms and the algorithm precisely enough to reimplement: whether it decimates (emits the first real fix at or after each boundary) or interpolates, what happens to the first and last point, and what happens when the native interval is already coarser than the target. It states the rationale in one sentence naming flight_points row-count consistency with the live recorder.
§4 states the hard cap on trackpoints accepted per file (before and/or after resampling) and the reject code for exceeding it.

§5 gives the formula for each of ground_speed_kts, heading_deg, vertical_speed_fpm, airspeed_kts and on_ground as a function of the previous and current resampled point, states which point of a pair the value is assigned to, and states what the FIRST point gets (it has no predecessor). It states explicitly that airspeed_kts carries ground speed because GPS has no air data, and that max_airspeed_kts on an imported flight is therefore a ground-speed maximum — the reason the source column exists.
§5 states the guard for dt <= 0 and the guard for an implausible derived value (a GPS glitch producing a 4000 kt segment), naming either a clamp, a warning, or an explicit decision to do neither.

§6 states how each closeFlight() argument is computed from the resampled points: end_time, arrival_lat/lon, duration_sec, distance_nm, max_altitude_ft, max_airspeed_kts, point_count. duration_sec must state whether it uses wall-clock (last ts minus first ts) or the sum-of-gaps-excluding-gaps-over-MAX_COUNTED_GAP_MS rule the live recorder uses at src/flightManager.ts:488-493, and why. It states that MAX_COUNTED_GAP_MS is copied into src/gpx.ts rather than imported, with the reason (importing flightManager would pull ./db into the pure module) and the src/geo.ts:1-14 deliberate-copy precedent.

§6 states that departure/arrival ICAO come from findNearestAirport() on the first and last resampled point with its default 10 nm radius, and what the flight row holds when no airport is within range (null, as the live path already does at src/flightManager.ts:240,294).

§7 specifies POST /api/flights/import/gpx completely: multipart field name, the dedicated multer instance name and its MAX_GPX_BYTES / MAX_GPX_FILES values, the optional `aircraft` (and any other) body fields and how they are trimmed and defaulted, the success status and body `{ imported, results }` with the exact per-file result object (filename, status, flight_id?, error?, warnings?), the failure statuses, and the behaviour when some files succeed and others fail. It states that a file that fails parsing must leave NO flight row behind, and names the mechanism (parse fully before the first insert, and/or a transaction).

§7 states where the route is registered in src/server.ts and why that position is safe: it must be ahead of app.get('*') (src/server.ts:776) and must not be shadowed by app.get/patch/delete('/api/flights/:id') (src/server.ts:317,325,355) or app.post('/api/flights/:id/flight-plan') (src/server.ts:365). Registering beside app.post('/api/flights/combine') (src/server.ts:152) is the suggested position; confirm or replace it.

§8 specifies the Home-page client contract: where the upload control sits relative to the existing flights-header and combine-toolbar, the file input attributes, the aircraft field, whether raw fetch or apiFetch is used and why (see the reasoning at client/src/pages/TripDetail.tsx:149-157 — a body that must be rendered on both 2xx and 4xx cannot go through apiFetch), the per-file result rendering, and the refresh call afterwards.

§8 specifies the provenance label: the badge text, the CSS class name following the existing .badge / .badge-* convention at client/src/index.css:397-431, and the two places it appears (the Home flight row and the FlightDetail header). It states what a 'simconnect' flight shows (nothing — the default is unlabelled).

§9 answers each of these explicitly: (a) what `source` the row produced by combineFlights() (src/db.ts:604) gets, given that it INSERTs a fresh row that would otherwise silently take the 'simconnect' default even when both inputs were GPX imports; (b) that a GPX import does NOT run the active-trip auto-link (src/flightManager.ts:244) and the user links a planned leg manually through the existing PUT /api/flights/:id/planned-leg; (c) that PDF export, the trip journey and the altitude chart need no change, or names the change; (d) that duplicate detection is out of scope for v1 and re-importing the same file creates a second flight.

§10 lists the fixture files T-002 must create under samples/gpx/synthetic/, one per rule in §3 and §4, each with its expected outcome (parsed with N points / rejected with code X), in the style of samples/lnmpln/synthetic/. Every reject code declared in §3 has at least one bad-*.gpx fixture, and there is at least one good multi-segment fixture and one good 1 Hz fixture whose resampled point count is stated as a number.
